findings.claim: Entry points are registered at install time; after adding or changing one, `uv sync` will not reinstall the package, so use `uv pip install -e .`. Repeated at project-setup:347, components.md:311 and :439, and in the failure-mode paragraph.
findings.evidence: Reproduced in a scratch copy with uv 0.13.6 / dagster-dg-cli 1.13.28: appended `[project.entry-points] "dagster_dg_cli.registry_modules" = { probe_proj = "probe_proj.components" }` to pyproject.toml, ran `uv sync`; output `Uninstalled 1 package / Installed 1 package / ~ probe-proj==0.1.0`, and `importlib.metadata.entry_points(group='dagster_dg_cli.registry_modules')` then listed the new entry point. The claim comes from the docs page migrating-project ('uv sync will not reinstall your package'), which is stale against current uv, whose default cache-keys include pyproject.toml.
findings.fix: Say: `uv sync` (or `uv run`) reinstalls the project when pyproject.toml entry points change; if `dg list registry-modules` still lacks the module, force it with `uv sync --reinstall-package <pkg>` or `uv pip install -e .`. Drop 'uv sync will not do it' everywhere.

findings.claim: Two mechanisms register components (registry_modules config, entry point) and the printed key is always the full dotted path including the defining module (e.g. my_project.components.shell_command.ShellCommand). Entry point is presented as the normal route (project-setup:164-171, migration section).
findings.evidence: create-dagster 1.13.28 generates pyproject with `registry_modules = ["demo_proj.components.*"]` and NO entry point. dagster_dg_core/component.py:48 `# Only load project plugin modules if there is no entry point`: once an entry point exists, `[tool.dg.project] registry_modules` is ignored. discover_entry_point_package_objects scans only the entry-point module's own namespace, so a class must be re-exported from components/__init__.py; `dg scaffold component Other` then appended `from probe_proj.components.other import Other as Other` and `dg list components --json` printed key `probe_proj.components.Other` (not ...other.Other). Both `probe_proj.components.Other` and `probe_proj.components.other.Other` pass `dg check yaml`/`dg check defs` as `type:`. Without an entry point, the wildcard config alone listed `probe_proj.components.shell_command.ShellCommand` after `dg scaffold component` with no reinstall.
findings.fix: State the rule: scaffolded projects use `registry_modules` in [tool.dg.project] and need no entry point or reinstall; add an entry point only for components shipped from an installed package, and know it silently disables registry_modules and requires re-exports in the module `__init__`. Replace 'copy type from dg list components; full dotted path' with 'any importable class path works; dg list components shows the registry key'.

findings.claim: State-backed component example: `@dataclass class MyStateBackedComponent(dg.StateBackedComponent)` with `defs_state: ResolvedDefsStateConfig = DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem()`.
findings.evidence: Ran the exact class in the 1.13.28 scratch project (Python 3.14): `ValueError: mutable default <class 'dagster.components.utils.defs_state.DefsStateConfigArgs'> for field defs_state is not allowed: use default_factory` (surfaces as an 'Entry point error' in every dg command). Python 3.11+ rejects unhashable dataclass defaults; the project supports 3.10-3.14. After switching to `field(default_factory=DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem)` it loaded but `dg check yaml` said `Additional properties are not allowed ('base_url' was unexpected)` until `dg.Resolvable` was added to the bases; `issubclass(dg.StateBackedComponent, dg.Resolvable)` is False. With both fixes `dg check defs` passed and `.local_defs_state` was written. The skill copied the broken example from the StateBackedComponent docstring.
findings.fix: Use `class X(dg.StateBackedComponent, dg.Resolvable)` as a dataclass, with `defs_state: ResolvedDefsStateConfig = field(default_factory=DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem)` (import `field`). Add a one-line note that StateBackedComponent is not Resolvable by itself.

findings.claim: 'Environment variables referenced in templates must exist at load time, not just run time.' Implies a missing variable fails the load.
findings.evidence: Scratch FunctionComponent with `description: "{{ env.MISSING_VAR_X }}"`, `group_name: "g_{{ env.MISSING_VAR_X }}"`, `requirements.env` declared, variable unset: `dg check yaml --validate-requirements` and `dg check defs` both succeed ('All definitions loaded successfully.'), and the resolved values were `None` (whole-value template) and `g_None` (interpolated). `dg list envs` shows an empty Value column. Setting the var gave the real value.
findings.fix: Replace with: an unset `{{ env.X }}` does not fail validation or load; it silently resolves to None / the string 'None'. `--validate-requirements` checks only that variables are declared, not that they are set. Use `dg list envs` to confirm values and `env('X', 'default')` or a template_var that raises when a value is mandatory.

findings.claim: post_processing settable attributes are listed, 'a later targeted entry refines a broad earlier one'; no mention of `operation`.
findings.evidence: dagster/components/resolved/core_models.py:394-424: AssetPostProcessorModel has `operation: Literal['merge','replace'] = 'merge'`; in merge mode only `metadata` and `tags` are merged and every other attribute is replaced. Reproduced: asset with kinds [a], tags {x:1}, deps [upstream] plus post_processing {kinds:[b], tags:{y:2}, deps:[other]} produced kinds {'b'}, tags {x,y,dagster/kind/b}, deps [other]. probes.question: In a Dagster 1.13 project, my component's defs.yaml uses `description: "token={{ env.API_TOKEN }}"` and API_TOKEN is not set anywhere. What do `dg check yaml --validate-requirements` and `dg check defs` do, and what ends up in the asset description?
probes.answer: Both pass. An unset `{{ env.X }}` does not fail at load; it silently renders as None (whole-value template) or the string 'None' inside an interpolated string, so the description becomes 'token=None'. --validate-requirements only checks that the variable is declared under requirements.env, not that it is set. Verified on dagster 1.13.28.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: It fails validation/load with a missing environment variable error (the skill itself says env vars 'must exist at load time').

probes.question: A defs/ module contains a module-level `@dg.asset` and also a `@dg.definitions` function returning `dg.Definitions(...)`. After `dg list defs`, which assets show up and is there a warning?
probes.answer: Only the assets in the Definitions returned by the @dg.definitions function load; the module-scope @dg.asset is skipped with no warning (reproduced). Keep @dg.definitions functions in their own module.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Both load and merge, or Dagster warns/raises about the duplicate or skipped definition.

probes.question: A defs.yaml has `post_processing: assets: [{attributes: {kinds: [b], tags: {y: '2'}}}]` and the component already sets `kinds: [a]` and `tags: {x: '1'}` on its asset. What are the final kinds and tags, and does `dg check yaml` validate the post_processing keys?
probes.answer: Default `operation: merge` merges only tags and metadata, so tags become {x, y} but kinds is replaced: {b} only (same for deps, owners, group_name). `operation: replace` replaces everything. `dg check yaml` does not validate post_processing contents (its schema is just `object`); bad keys such as key_prefix fail only in `dg check defs`.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: kinds {a, b} (merged) and `dg check yaml` catches bad post_processing attributes.

probes.question: I wrote a custom StateBackedComponent as `@dataclass class X(dg.StateBackedComponent)` with `defs_state: ResolvedDefsStateConfig = DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem()` (copied from the Dagster docstring) and every dg command now errors. What is wrong and what is the fix?
probes.answer: Dataclasses on Python 3.11+ reject the unhashable pydantic default: `ValueError: mutable default ... DefsStateConfigArgs ... use default_factory`. Use `field(default_factory=DefsStateConfigArgs.local_filesystem)`. Also add `dg.Resolvable` to the bases, because StateBackedComponent is not Resolvable and otherwise defs.yaml attributes are rejected ('Additional properties are not allowed').
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Suggests a missing entry point/reinstall, or a wrong management_type enum, or that the snippet is fine as written.

probes.question: I added a `[project.entry-points] "dagster_dg_cli.registry_modules"` entry to pyproject.toml of my uv-managed Dagster project. Do I need `uv pip install -e .`, and what happens to the `registry_modules` list in [tool.dg.project]?
probes.answer: With current uv, plain `uv sync` detects the pyproject change and reinstalls the package, registering the entry point (verified, uv 0.13.6). Once an entry point exists, dg ignores `[tool.dg.project] registry_modules` entirely, and discovers only objects exposed in the entry-point module's own namespace (so classes must be re-exported in components/__init__.py, which `dg scaffold component` then does). Scaffolded projects don't need an entry point at all.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: 'uv sync will not reinstall the package; you must run uv pip install -e .' and that both mechanisms are combined.

probes.question: My `dg check defs` in CI behaves differently from production because code branches on `os.getenv('DAGSTER_IS_DEV_CLI')`. Why, and which dg commands set that variable?
probes.answer: The top-level `dg` group sets DAGSTER_IS_DEV_CLI=1 for every dg command (check defs, list defs, launch, check yaml...), not just `dg dev` (also set by `dagster dev`). `dg check defs` additionally sets DAGSTER_IS_DEFS_VALIDATION_CLI=1.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Only `dg dev` sets DAGSTER_IS_DEV_CLI, so `dg check defs` sees the production code path.

probes.question: I call `defs.map_asset_specs(lambda spec: spec.replace_attributes(partitions_def=pdef))` inside a Component.build_defs override. What happens in 1.13.28?
probes.answer: TypeError: `Definitions.map_asset_specs()` takes 1 positional argument but 2 were given; the signature is keyword-only (`func=`, optional `selection=`). It is also a preview API (PreviewWarning).
probes.wrong_answer_trap: It works and returns a Definitions with the mapped specs.

probes.question: Which launcher does `dg launch --assets 'key:"customers"'` use, and will the resulting run appear in the UI of a `dg dev` instance I have running in another terminal?
probes.answer: `dg launch` does not use the instance run launcher or the daemon: it executes the selection in-process (it calls the `dagster asset materialize` / job execute implementation), requires exactly one of --assets or --job, works only in a project context (not workspaces or Dagster+), and writes to its own ephemeral temp instance (`.tmp_dagster_home_*`) unless DAGSTER_HOME is shared, so it won't show up in an unrelated `dg dev` UI.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: It submits a run to the running dg dev instance through the run launcher, visible in its UI, and can target workspaces or Dagster+ deployments.

The 'one step and seven materializations' sentence at L200 is only true under that precondition.
findings.evidence: dagster_dg_cli/cli/launch.py calls asset_materialize_command_impl in-process (source comment: 'executes the selected assets in process'). dagster/_cli/asset.py:165-178 raises: 'Partition ranges with the CLI require all selected assets to have a BackfillPolicy.single_run() policy ... Assets without this policy would require creating a backfill ... which needs a running daemon'. Ran `dg launch -f assets.py --assets multi --partition-range 2024-05-01...2024-05-07` (multi_run(3)) and the same for a default-policy asset: both CheckError. With single_run over 3 days: 1 STEP_SUCCESS and 3 ASSET_MATERIALIZATION events.
findings.fix: State that `dg launch --partition-range` is a local in-process run that requires single_run() on every selected asset and errors otherwise; multi-run and default-policy backfills go through the UI or `dagster job backfill` with a daemon.

probes.answer: It fails with a CheckError. `dg launch` runs in-process (no daemon, no backfill) and --partition-range requires every selected asset to have BackfillPolicy.single_run(); multi_run or the default one-run-per-partition policy are rejected and need the UI or `dagster job backfill` with a daemon.

probes.question: An asset uses backfill_policy=dg.BackfillPolicy.single_run() with a daily partitions_def. In the body I call context.partition_key and return a DataFrame. What goes wrong when it is backfilled over several days, and how do you fix it?
probes.answer: Two failures: context.partition_key raises DagsterInvariantViolationError for a run covering a range (use partition_time_window, partition_key_range or partition_keys), and returning a value fails at handle-output because the default filesystem I/O manager cannot persist one object for multiple partitions. Write the data yourself and return None or dg.MaterializeResult(metadata=...). A 3-day range logs 1 step and 3 materializations.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Thinking Dagster fans the value out per partition or that partition_key returns the first key.

probes.question: A daily-partitioned asset has a schedule built with build_schedule_from_partitioned_job(job, hour_of_day=1, minute_of_hour=30). On 2024-05-20 at 01:30 the tick fires. Which partition does it run, and what changes the answer?
probes.answer: 2024-05-19, the latest completed partition (default end_offset=0). Setting end_offset=1 on the DailyPartitionsDefinition makes the same tick run 2024-05-20. hour_of_day/minute_of_hour only shift tick time, not the chosen partition.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Running the partition for the current date (2024-05-20), or adjusting hour_of_day to change which partition is selected.

probes.question: A downstream daily asset takes `up: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]` from an hourly upstream using a UPathIOManager-based I/O manager (the default filesystem one). Only 3 of the 24 hourly partitions for the day exist. What happens, and how do you let the downstream run?
probes.answer: Loading raises (FileNotFoundError, wrapped in DagsterExecutionLoadInputError) because missing partitions are errors by default. Put allow_missing_partitions=True in the consuming input's metadata: ins={'up': dg.AssetIn(metadata={'allow_missing_partitions': True})}; the dict then contains just the 3 present keys.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: That the input silently contains whatever exists, or that the flag goes on the upstream asset or I/O manager config.

probes.question: Inside an I/O manager's load_input, I want the table name stored in the upstream asset's metadata, and also a value that the upstream asset reported via MaterializeResult(metadata=...). What do context.definition_metadata, context.upstream_output.definition_metadata and context.upstream_output.output_metadata give me?
probes.answer: InputContext.definition_metadata is the metadata on the consuming AssetIn/In (not the upstream asset's). upstream_output.definition_metadata is the upstream asset's definition metadata (use it for table names). upstream_output.output_metadata is {} during load_input: runtime metadata from MaterializeResult/Output is event-log only and not visible to I/O managers.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: That context.definition_metadata in load_input holds the upstream asset's metadata, and that MaterializeResult metadata can be read back via upstream_output.output_metadata.

probes.question: An asset is declared with @dg.asset(output_required=False) and I want it to skip materialization on some runs. My function does `if nothing_new: return None`. Does that skip materialization?

Only a generator that yields nothing (or yields conditionally) skips: with `return` I got 1 materialization event, with a generator that yields nothing I got 0.

probes.question: I define a WeeklyPartitionsDefinition(start_date="2024-05-01") (a Wednesday) with default settings. What is the first partition key, and how do I cover the days from May 1 onward?

probes.answer: No. In 1.13.28 `dg launch` runs the job (or asset materialization) synchronously in the local CLI process via `dagster job execute` / `asset materialize`, using the job's executor. It blocks until the run finishes and does not use the instance's run launcher or daemon. The CLI option is `--job`; `--jobs` is rejected.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: It submits the run asynchronously through the configured run launcher and returns immediately (this is what the docs, and ops-jobs-and-graphs.md:260, say).

probes.question: In Dagster 1.13 I have a daily partitioned job and a hand-written schedule. How do I compute 'the latest partition key as of this tick' for `RunRequest(partition_key=...)`, and what must I not pass?
probes.answer: Wrap the lookup in `with dg.partition_loading_context(effective_dt=context.scheduled_execution_time): key = partitions_def.get_last_partition_key()`. `get_last_partition_key()` takes no arguments in 1.13.28, and `current_time=` raises a TypeError.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: `partitions_def.get_last_partition_key(current_time=context.scheduled_execution_time)`, the older signature.

probes.question: I have a `@dg.run_failure_sensor` in code location `alerts` that should also watch jobs in code location `analytics`. I set `monitored_jobs=[dg.CodeLocationSelector(location_name='analytics')]`. Will failures of jobs in `alerts` still trigger it?
probes.answer: No. Once `monitored_jobs` is set, same-location runs match only listed job definitions or selectors, so a list of only other locations' selectors stops watching the home location. Add `dg.CodeLocationSelector(location_name='alerts')` too. Setting both `monitored_jobs` and `monitor_all_code_locations=True` raises 'Cannot specify both'.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: The selectors add to the default own-location monitoring, so `alerts` is still covered.

probes.question: I want a downstream asset to materialize only after all three of its upstream assets have updated each cycle. Which built-in AutomationCondition do I use, and which one is the common wrong choice?
probes.answer: Use `AutomationCondition.on_cron(cron)`; its cron tick acts as a synchronization barrier and it requires every upstream to update within the tick. `eager()` fires when any dependency updates. Do not hand-build 'all_deps_match(newly_updated().since(...))', which has no barrier and can desynchronize indefinitely. `on_cron` also defaults to UTC unless `cron_timezone` is passed.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: `eager()` (it triggers on any upstream), or a custom `all_deps_match(newly_updated())` condition.

probes.question: I subclassed `dg.AutomationCondition` with a custom `evaluate()` and attached it to an asset. It never evaluates, or errors in the daemon. What do I have to add, and what are the limits?
probes.answer: Custom Python conditions only evaluate on a sensor with `use_user_code_server=True` (e.g. `AutomationConditionSensorDefinition(name, target=..., use_user_code_server=True)`), since the daemon can't import user code. That sensor is capped at 500 assets/checks, is beta, and cannot target asset jobs. `default_condition` is only valid with `use_user_code_server=True`.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: The default_automation_condition_sensor evaluates custom conditions automatically once toggled on, or a plain @dg.sensor can evaluate them.

probes.question: Using Dagster 1.13 declarative automation with `eager()` on a daily-partitioned asset, 30 historical partitions are missing. How many partitions does eager request, and how do I make it cover older ones?
probes.answer: Only the latest time partition, because eager/on_cron/on_missing all start with `in_latest_time_window()`. To widen, `.without(AutomationCondition.in_latest_time_window())` or `.replace(in_latest_time_window(), in_latest_time_window(timedelta(days=N)))` (string-label replace also works). Static and dynamic partitions are not limited to the latest.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: It requests all missing partitions (a backfill), or the fix is a backfill policy.

probes.question: An op is annotated `-> tuple[dg.Output[int], dg.Output[str]]` and returns `dg.Output(1), dg.Output('a')`. Why does the job fail with a type check error, and what do I change?
probes.answer: Without `out={'a': dg.Out(), 'b': dg.Out()}` the op has a single output `result` typed as a tuple, so each Output object fails the int/str type check (`DagsterTypeCheckDidNotPass`). The return annotation does not create multiple outputs; declare `out={...}`. With `out` declared the same body works.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: The tuple-of-Output annotation alone declares two outputs.

probes.question: A graph op is decorated with `retry_policy=RetryPolicy(max_retries=3)` and raises `dg.Failure('bad input', allow_retries=False)`. How many times does the op body run, and how many with a plain `dg.Failure('bad input')`?

probes.answer: Two problems: passing an explicit IO manager to materialize_to_memory raises DagsterInvariantViolationError (it forces mem_io_manager); and with a parameter dependency the upstream asset definition must be in the list or you get DagsterInvalidDefinitionError 'Input asset ... is not produced by any of the provided asset ops'. probes.question: An `@dg.asset_check(asset=orders, blocking=True)` returns `AssetCheckResult(passed=False)`; another returns `passed=False, severity=WARN`. In a job that also materializes a downstream asset of `orders`, what runs and what does `dg.materialize(...)` do with default arguments?
probes.answer: ERROR-severity (default) failure: the check step fails with DagsterAssetCheckFailedError ('1 blocking asset check failed with ERROR severity'), downstream assets do not execute, and dg.materialize raises that error because raise_on_error=True by default (use raise_on_error=False to inspect). WARN severity never blocks: downstream runs and the run succeeds.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Thinking any failed blocking check stops downstream regardless of severity, or that a check failure only flags the UI and downstream still runs.

probes.answer: `AssetSelection.assets(orders)` automatically includes checks attached to those assets (and `dg launch --assets orders` runs them too). Use `.without_checks()` on the selection for the asset job and `dg.AssetSelection.checks_for_assets(orders)` for a separate check job, each with its own ScheduleDefinition.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Assuming a selection of assets excludes checks and that checks must be explicitly added to run alongside the asset.

No sensor or schedule is required, unlike build_last_update_freshness_checks. The pre-1.6 class was renamed LegacyFreshnessPolicy; the name FreshnessPolicy now refers to the new API (time_window with fail_window >= 60s and warn_window < fail_window, or cron).

probes.question: I need a resource that wraps a foreign client class (e.g. `GitHub(token)`) with a config field, and an asset that receives the built client. Which base class and annotation do I use in Dagster 1.13 given the docs mention `ConfigurableResourceFactory` and `dg.Resource[T]`?
probes.answer: Subclass `dg.ConfigurableResource[GitHub]` and implement `create_resource(self, context) -> GitHub`; annotate the asset parameter `dg.ResourceParam[GitHub]`. `dg.ConfigurableResourceFactory` and `dg.Resource` are not exported from dagster in 1.13.28 (hasattr returns False), even though some docs pages use those names.

probes.question: In run-config YAML for an asset whose Config has an `enum.Enum` field and a pydantic discriminated union (`pet: Cat | Dog = Field(discriminator='pet_type')`), how are the enum value and the union written, and what happens with unknown keys?
probes.answer: Enums are written by member name (`Bob: GUEST`, not the value `guest`; the value form raises DagsterInvalidConfigError). A discriminated union nests under the discriminator value (`pet: {cat: {meows: 10}}`; the flat `{pet_type: cat, meows: 10}` form fails). Unknown keys fail with DagsterInvalidConfigError unless the model subclasses dg.PermissiveConfig. Asset config lives under `ops: {<asset_name>: {config: ...}}` and dg.RunConfig's first positional argument is `ops`.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Writing the enum's value and the flat pydantic-style union form, or expecting extra keys to be silently ignored.

probes.question: I changed `[tool.dg.project]` settings and need `dg` to use a non-default virtualenv, e.g. `../.venvs/my-project`. Where must I set `DG_PROJECT_PYTHON_EXECUTABLE` for it to take effect, and does exporting it in my shell work?
probes.answer: It must be in the project-root `.env` file (relative paths resolve against the project root). dg reads it via dotenv_values on `<project_root>/.env` only (dagster_dg_core/context.py project_python_executable); exporting it in the shell has no effect. Default is `<project_root>/.venv`, and `--use-active-venv` is the alternative.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Exporting the variable in the shell or setting it in pyproject.toml.

probes.question: In a Dagster 1.13 asset job, a non-blocking asset check on asset `a` returns `AssetCheckResult(passed=False, severity=AssetCheckSeverity.ERROR)`. With `blocking=True` and ERROR severity, the check step raises DagsterAssetCheckFailedError, the run fails and downstream assets are skipped. Verified with `dg.materialize`.

probes.question: A dbt microbatch incremental model is wired to a Dagster daily-partitioned `@dbt_assets`. Which CLI flags should the asset body pass for the partition window, and what happens if you pass `--vars` start_date/end_date instead?
probes.answer: Pass `--event-time-start` and `--event-time-end` (taken from `context.partition_time_window`). `--vars` only injects values into the SQL template and does not control batch scheduling, so the model silently processes every batch from `begin` to now. Confirmed on the Dagster docs dbt-patterns page.
probes.wrong_answer_trap: Use `--vars` with start_date/end_date like a regular incremental model, since that restricts the window.

probes.question: With dagster-fivetran, what is the default effect of Dagster triggering a connector sync on the connector's Fivetran schedule, and which two `FivetranWorkspace` settings change the default behaviors around that sync?
